summary:
The Winnebago Land Transfer Act of 2023, Pub. L. No. 118-68, directs the trust treatment and reservation status of specified Federal lands for the benefit of the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska. Section 1 provides the short title.

Section 2(a), subject to all valid existing rights, declares that all right, title, and interest of the United States, including improvements and appurtenances, in the Federal lands described in § 2(b) are part of the Winnebago Reservation created by the 1865 Treaty between the United States and the Winnebago Tribe. It further provides that those lands shall be held in trust by the United States for the benefit of the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska, subject to the same terms and conditions as the lands described in the Treaty with the Winnebago Tribe, 1865, 14 Stat. 671. The Act does not amend any provision of the United States Code, and it contains no separate authorization of appropriations or direct appropriation.

Section 2(b) identifies the covered Federal lands by reference to condemnation and taking records filed in Federal district court proceedings. The lands consist of: (1) the specified portion of Tract No. 119, as filed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Iowa, Western Division, Civil Case No. 70-C-3015-W, executed May 11, 1973, located in portions of Sections 8, 9, 16, and 17, Township 86 North, Range 47 West of the Fifth Principal Meridian, Woodbury County, Iowa, subject to the described Nebraska/Iowa State Line and Winnebago Reservation boundary limitations; (2) Tract No. 210, as described in Schedule “A” to the referenced declaration of taking, legal description, judgment on stipulation, and order of distribution filed in the same Iowa action; and (3) Tract No. 113, as described in the referenced judgment on declaration of taking and legal description filed in the United States District Court for the District of Nebraska, Civ. No. 03498.

Section 2(c) imposes a permanent gaming restriction: class II and class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, 25 U.S.C. 2701 et seq., is prohibited at any time on the lands taken into trust under § 2(a). The Act contains no delayed effective date and therefore took effect upon enactment on July 12, 2024.
